restrained-satire.voice_reason: Z, like the reference, lets flat physical detail and bystanders' indifference carry the judgment (the re-glued envelope, the dust on the bench, the ticked attendance column) with no narrator commentary, while X keeps stepping in to point the meaning with essayistic asides, a sentimental fingertip-on-the-letter beat and an aphoristic closing line.
restrained-satire.notes: V, W and X share most of their sentences; V is the leanest of the three but pastes the reference's 『』 quotation marks as surface mimicry; W and X add the same sentimental shoe-repair visit and fingertip line, X further adds the '像怕吵醒什么' aside, so W and X are nearly indistinguishable. Z and Y are close at the top: Y has the sharpest satirical devices (supplier's rationale, framed zero, the auntie thanked for searching her bag) but Z is colder and is the only draft that keeps the material's sequence of selecting '已了解' alone before leaving work, after the old man is gone; V/W/X/Y move the selection to the afternoon in the old man's presence. I judged that timing shift a change of staging rather than of outcome, so it is not listed as a fact violation, but it is why Z edges Y overall.
